aria: Animated recap of the Bulls' 107 to 105 win at Charlotte: Josh Giddey's driving floater with 1:32 left that made it 100 to 97, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Matas Buzelis' 24 points, the top scorers, how the Bulls won, and the next game.

figure.label: Josh Giddey, listed 6-7, 214 lb (Basketball-Reference); no sourced wingspan

notes: Box score from Land of Basketball's game page for the Bulls' 107–105 win at Charlotte on Nov 25, 2026: all 107 Chicago points and all 105 Charlotte points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (39 of 78, 13 of 31 from three, 16 of 20 FT for Chicago; 36 of 87, 11 of 34, 22 of 26 for Charlotte), assists (25–20), steals (5–7) and blocks (7–3). The final and the quarter scores (21–25–27–34 to 23–25–23–34) also match the Covers matchup page, the AP story and Hoops Nightly; 48–46 Charlotte at the half is in the AP, and 73–71 Chicago after three in Yardbarker. Bench points (42–22), second-chance points (7–22) and the biggest lead for each side (8) are from Hoops Nightly; Bleacher Nation also says neither team led by more than eight. The 22 lead changes are in the AP, Yardbarker and Rookie Wire. Records are from Covers and the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Matas Buzelis had 24 points on 8 of 15 shooting and 8 of 9 free throws, his fourth 20-point game in his last six (Bleacher Nation). Seven Bulls scored 10 or more (Rookie Wire; the box score). Chicago has won two straight and is 2–2 in NBA Cup group play (AP). Brandon Miller scored 35 for Charlotte, his fourth 30-point game of the season (AP). Late: Nic Claxton's cutting dunk from Giddey at 2:30 put Chicago ahead 98–97 for good; Buzelis tipped in a weakside rebound with 23.2 seconds left for 104–101 (AP); Coby White's last shot rimmed out at the buzzer (AP). Next: Chicago hosts Indiana on Saturday, the first of a six-game home stand (Bleacher Nation); Charlotte hosts Brooklyn on Saturday (Covers).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Josh Giddey's 8-foot driving floating bank shot with 1:32 left that made it 100–97: the Hoops Nightly and Digest Sports play-by-play both have it at 1:32 for 100–97, after Claxton's dunk made it 98–97 at 2:30. So the board's Bulls +1 to +3 is 98–97 to 100–97. No assist is listed and the defender isn't described, so it is drawn as the template's plain drive to a short finish. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Chicago Bulls or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Giddey's listed 6-foot-7 and 214 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms at the default length because no wingspan is reported there, in the Bulls' road kit with No. 3 (Basketball-Reference) and a lighter skin tone; he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
